title.zh: 各向异性压强环向电流分解

summary: Project axisymmetric gyrotropic pressure force onto toroidal current and separate the isotropic perpendicular-pressure contribution from the anisotropic remainder.

identity.relation: R-Z poloidal field and gyrotropic pressures to toroidal current density and two additive contributions
identity.direction: R-Z grid, B_R, B_Z, p_parallel, p_perp -> j_phi, gradp_term, anisotropy_curvature_term, B
identity.definition: Evaluate the maintained gyrotropic force-balance projection twice: once with supplied p_parallel and p_perp and once with p_parallel=p_perp. The latter J_phi is gradp_term; anisotropy_curvature_term is the full J_phi minus gradp_term. The decomposition is defined by this discrete difference, not an independently discretized curvature formula.
identity.model: axisymmetric gyrotropic pressure tensor and perpendicular current projection
identity.geometry: rectilinear cylindrical R-Z grid with at least three nodes per axis
identity.coordinates: arrays indexed [Z,R]; R nonnegative and both axes strictly increasing
identity.boundary: The bound force kernel uses regular-axis tensor limits and reports the parallel force separately; its toroidal projection alone is not a complete equilibrium.
assumptions: Both magnetic components and pressures refer to the same R-Z nodes and use T and Pa, respectively.
The parallel/perpendicular distinction is meaningful for the caller's gyrotropic model.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.constraints: Rectilinear, nonnegative R, strictly increasing radial axis and at least three columns; same shape as other arrays.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.constraints: Rectilinear, strictly increasing axial axis and at least three rows; same shape as other arrays.

inputs.name: br
inputs.constraints: Exact grid shape; zero or tiny fields follow the dependency's numerical convention, not a physical validity gate.

inputs.name: bz
inputs.constraints: Exact grid shape and co-located with br.

inputs.name: p_parallel
inputs.description: Pressure parallel to the poloidal field.
inputs.constraints: Exact grid shape and nonnegative; scalar broadcasting is not performed.

inputs.name: p_perp
inputs.description: Pressure perpendicular to the poloidal field.
inputs.constraints: Exact grid shape and nonnegative; also supplies both pressures in the isotropic comparison.

outputs.name: j_phi
outputs.constraints: Equals gradp_term plus anisotropy_curvature_term by construction; zero at an R=0 axis column.

outputs.name: gradp_term
outputs.description: Toroidal current from the isotropic p_perp comparison.
outputs.constraints: Exactly the dependency's J_phi with both pressure inputs set to p_perp; not an independently evaluated gradient.

outputs.name: anisotropy_curvature_term
outputs.description: Difference between full and isotropic-comparison current.
outputs.constraints: Computed as j_phi - gradp_term; zero for equal pressures up to arithmetic error.

outputs.name: B
outputs.description: Magnitude of the supplied poloidal field.
outputs.constraints: Taken from the full force-balance evaluation.

outputs.name: force_diagnostics
outputs.description: Full corrected tensor-force result, including raw and resolved compatibility diagnostics.
outputs.constraints: Full corrected tensor-force result, including raw and resolved compatibility diagnostics.

preconditions: All six arrays satisfy the exact shape, grid and pressure requirements of the bound anisotropic force-balance Operator.
The caller has a physically meaningful co-located axisymmetric gyrotropic pressure and field state.
supported: Discrete total and isotropic-comparison toroidal current on the stated R-Z grid; constant pressure, radial isotropic-gradient and rotating-field anisotropic examples are directly tested.
excluded: An independent analytic curvature formula or proof of parallel force balance.
Non-axisymmetric geometry, toroidal-field contribution or a complete equilibrium solver.
Masking current outside plasma cells; the caller must do that separately.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: The bound force-balance Operator raises ValueError for nonfinite, wrong-rank or mismatched arrays; invalid R-Z grid, negative pressure or insufficient samples. Both evaluations use active_mask=None.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Dependency and arithmetic failures propagate; extreme finite inputs are not guaranteed to yield finite projected currents.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this Operator performs no iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned if either force-balance evaluation fails.

example.description: An isotropic pressure increasing linearly in R gives an analytic current in a uniform 2 T axial field.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.equilibrium import compute_anisotropic_toroidal_current
r, z = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(0.2, 0.5, 5), np.linspace(-0.2, 0.2, 4))
p = 3.0 + r
result = compute_anisotropic_toroidal_current(r, z, np.zeros_like(r), np.full_like(r, 2.0), p, p)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['j_phi'], 0.5)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['gradp_term'], 0.5)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['anisotropy_curvature_term'], 0.0, atol=1e-12)
example.expected: The full and isotropic-comparison currents are 0.5 A/m^2, with zero anisotropic difference to tolerance.

scope: Manufactured radial perpendicular-pressure gradient and isotropic decomposition.
Rotating constant-magnitude field produces a nonzero anisotropic difference.
The R=0 axis column is zero, and invalid negative pressure is rejected.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Manufactured and analytic discrete checks establish only the stated poloidal model and declared integration geometry. Arbitrary Green matrices, pressure closures, experimental plasma applicability and public release are not established by these tests.
known_limitations: Caller-supplied physical closures and Green responses require their own evidence and coherent psi=R A_phi (Wb/rad) normalization.
Floating-point rounding envelopes do not bound discretization error or experimental uncertainty.
No expert scientific endorsement or public release follows from this numerical successor.
